title: Set up Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL

prerequisites.label: A GCP project is selected
prerequisites.hint: Check the project picker in the console top bar.

prerequisites.label: Billing is enabled on the project
prerequisites.hint: Cloud SQL instances bill while they run — even small ones.

prerequisites.label: The Cloud Console is open in this window
Console language is English
prerequisites.hint: Baymax finds buttons by their English names.

nextSteps: Wait for the instance status to turn green in the Cloud SQL list (a few minutes).
Keep your postgres password safe — you'll need it to connect.
Create a database and user for your app (Databases / Users tabs).
Stop or delete the instance when you no longer need it — it bills while running.

steps.title: Search for Cloud SQL
steps.description: Click the search bar at the top of the console and type "Cloud SQL". You can find any GCP product this way.
steps.selector: input.pcc-search-input, input[placeholder*="Search" i], input[aria-label*="search for resources" i]

steps.title: Open SQL from the results
steps.description: Click the "Cloud SQL" result (the Product) to open the Cloud SQL page.
steps.name: Cloud SQL
steps.revealSelector: input.pcc-search-input, input[placeholder*="Search" i], input[aria-label*="search for resources" i]

steps.title: Create an instance
steps.description: You're in Cloud SQL now. Click "Create instance" to start a new database.
steps.name: Create instance
steps.selector: a[href*="/sql/choose-instance-engine"], button[aria-label*="Create instance" i], a[aria-label*="Create instance" i]

steps.title: Start a new instance
steps.description: If a menu appears, choose "New instance" to create a fresh database.
steps.name: New instance

steps.title: Choose PostgreSQL
steps.description: Select PostgreSQL as the database engine for your new instance.
steps.name: PostgreSQL

steps.title: Name your instance
steps.description: Enter an instance ID, for example "baymax-postgres".
steps.name: Instance ID

steps.title: Set a password
steps.description: Enter a password for the default postgres user. Make sure to remember it — you'll need it to connect later.
steps.name: Password

steps.title: Choose a region
steps.description: Pick the region closest to you, for example asia-southeast1.
steps.name: Region

steps.title: Choose the Enterprise edition
steps.description: Pick the "Enterprise" edition — it is cheaper than Enterprise Plus. To shrink it further, set the "Edition preset" dropdown above to "Sandbox" (the smallest, lowest-cost size for development).
steps.name: Enterprise

steps.title: Create the instance
steps.description: Click "Create instance" to start provisioning your PostgreSQL database. This can take a few minutes.
steps.name: Create instance
